title: Welcome to my interactive CV
excerpt: This is the first post detailing the architecture and design decisions behind this cv.
content:
Building an interactive CV is an interesting challenge.

## Why an interactive CV?

Traditional resumes are static and often fail to convey the depth of a developer's experience. An interactive CV allows me to:
- Showcase my **skills** in a real-world application.
- Provide a more engaging experience for recruiters and engineering managers.
- Experiment with new technologies like **Next.js 16** and **React Server Components**.

### Core Technologies

1. Next.js App Router for dynamic routing.
2. Tailwind CSS v4 for rapid and modern styling.
3. Framer Motion for subtle micro-interactions.

Here is a snippet of my `page.js` component:

```javascript
export default function Home() {
  return (
    <main className="flex flex-col items-center">
      <Header />
      <Timeline title="Professional Path" items={professionalPath} />
    </main>
  );
}
```

I hope you enjoy exploring the different sections as much as I enjoyed building them!

title: Automating workflows with GitHub Actions
excerpt: A deep dive into how I automated our CI/CD pipelines.
content:
Automation is key in modern software development. Time spent on repetitive tasks is time taken away from building features.

## CI/CD Pipeline

My typical GitHub Actions workflow includes several essential jobs:

| Job Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Linting** | Runs ESLint and Prettier to ensure code consistency. |
| **Testing** | Executes the Jest test suite to check for regressions. |
| **Build** | Creates the production build of the Next.js application. |

Here's an example of a simple GitHub Actions YAML configuration:

```yaml
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Use Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20.x'
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run test
```

Automating the deployments means I can confidently merge PRs, knowing that checks will ensure only passing code hits production.
